body.en: For a parametric curve, \( \dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{dy/dt}{dx/dt} \). Polar area is \( \displaystyle A=\tfrac12\int_\alpha^\beta r^2\,d\theta. \)

The ratio test: \( \sum a_n \) converges absolutely if \( \displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}\Big|\dfrac{a_{n+1}}{a_n}\Big|<1 \). Taylor series and their intervals of convergence are the centrepiece of Unit 10.
AP Calculus BC extends AB with additional integration techniques, convergence tests, parametric/polar calculus, and infinite series — approximately 40% of the exam is BC-exclusive material.

label.en: 🎯 The AB Subscore & Strategic Scoring in BC

body.en:
• Two Scores from One Exam: Every student taking AP Calculus BC receives both an overall BC Exam Score (1–5) and an AB Subscore (1–5) based solely on the ~60% of the exam covering AB topics (Units 1–8).
  • The College Credit Safety Net: Most colleges award Calculus I credit for an AB Subscore of 4 or 5, even if your composite BC score is lower. Mastering core AB calculus provides an unbeatable foundation for both scores.
  • Predictable BC FRQ Real Estate: The 6 Free Response questions always dedicate exactly 2 questions to BC-only material: typically FRQ 2 or 5 on Parametric/Vector Motion or Polar Area, and FRQ 6 on Taylor Series and Error Bounds.

• 1. Parametric Second Derivative: Differentiate \( \frac{dy}{dx} \) with respect to \( t \), then divide by \( \frac{dx}{dt} \). Never divide second derivatives directly: \( \frac{d^2y}{dx^2} \neq \frac{y''(t)}{x''(t)} \).
  • 2. Lagrange vs. Alternating Error Bound: If an FRQ explicitly requires the Lagrange Error Bound, quoting the alternating series test bound (first omitted term) receives zero credit for the error bound point.
  • 3. Evaluating Limits for Improper Integrals: On Section II, you must write \( \lim_{b\to\infty}\int_a^b \) rather than plugging in \( \infty \) as an endpoint.

caption.en: Taylor polynomial approximations to $f(x) = e^x$ centered at $x = 0$. As the polynomial degree increases from $P_1(x) = 1 + x$ to $P_2(x) = 1 + x + \frac{1}{2}x^2$, the polynomial matches higher derivatives and hugs the exponential curve with rapidly diminishing error near the center.

question.en: A particle moves in the \(xy\)-plane with position given by \(x(t) = t^3 - 3t\) and \(y(t) = 2t^2 + 1\) for \(t > 0\). Find the slope of the tangent line \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) at \(t = 2\).

solution.en: Compute individual derivatives: \(\frac{dx}{dt} = 3t^2 - 3\) and \(\frac{dy}{dt} = 4t\). At \(t = 2\), \(\frac{dx}{dt} = 3(4) - 3 = 9\) and \(\frac{dy}{dt} = 4(2) = 8\). The parametric slope is \(\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{dy/dt}{dx/dt} = \frac{8}{9}\).
